correctness.rationale: The Boolean subalgebra generated by the finitely many subformula values is finite. Greedy atom selection separates at most t+1 values using at most t atoms. Injectivity on those original values makes every projected unary table assignment functional. Completing undefined unary entries using Boolean complement or bottom preserves both defining BALFI identities and all designated evaluations. Polynomial-time whole-bit-vector checks are equivalent to extendable partial BALFI tables. A standard hardness result yields coNP-completeness. checker.py successfully checked 41,568 exhaustive small cases, 2,000 deterministic random cases, and a separate necessity witness. Finite checks supplement, not replace, the all-size proof.

originality.rationale: The 2026 full-text finite filtration gives an upper bound of 2-EXPTIME and a coNP lower bound but no explicit linear-atom countermodel construction. Earlier algebraic embedding into non-normal modal fusions and 2023 coNP results for those fusions constitute a serious possible implication path for the complexity corollary. The claimed structural content is the direct m<=t BALFI reduction with explicit partial-table completion and polynomial native-language certificate; inspected sources did not state or immediately entail this precise claim. Absolute priority is not guaranteed.
residual_risks: The combination of the 2020/2022 modal embedding and 2023 coNP fusion results might yield an efficient shared-subformula reduction and establish the complexity corollary by prior methods.

Other older results on unary Boolean algebra expansions or neighbourhood modal filtration could imply the linear-atom separation lemma in different terminology; inspected results do not resolve absolute priority.

value.rationale: The 2026 RmbC paper presents a major gap between its upper and lower complexity bounds; closing it with an explicit natively checkable polynomial witness is an identified motivating problem. The distinguishing-coordinate proof is structural, preserves the full equality pattern required by nonclassical unary operations, and addresses a genuine pitfall of a naive one-world projection, demonstrated by an explicit four-element example. The result does not depend for its motivation on arbitrary chosen small parameters.
